lesson.title: Bone structure and connections between bones
lesson.summary: Bone shape predicts broad mechanical roles, but size alone does not define the category: phalanges are long bones despite being small.
tags: Bone structure and connections between bones
lesson.section: 1. Classification of Bones; 2. Connections Between Bones

steps.title: Classification of Bones
steps.body:
Bones form the rigid framework of the body. They protect organs, provide levers for muscles, store minerals, and contain marrow. In an oral exam, classify the bone first, then give its functional reason.

Long bones act as levers and have a shaft with two ends. Short bones provide compact stability. Flat bones protect and provide broad muscle attachment. Irregular bones have complex topographic shapes. Sesamoid bones develop in tendons and improve leverage. Pneumatic bones contain air-filled cavities.

steps.title: Connections Between Bones
steps.body:
Bone connections are either continuous or discontinuous. Continuous connections have no true cavity; synovial joints have an articular cavity and allow movement.

Syndesmosis is fibrous connection. Synchondrosis is cartilage connection. Symphysis is fibrocartilage connection. Synostosis is bone fusion. Synovial joints are discontinuous joints with a cavity.

steps.title: Why is structural classification useful before discussing movement?
steps.body: Structural classes identify what joins the bones and whether a cavity exists. Fibrous joints can range from nearly immobile sutures to more permissive syndesmoses; cartilaginous joints also differ in function. Synovial shape influences potential movement, but ligaments, capsule and muscles determine what is actually permitted. A pivot-shaped surface alone does not make a joint freely rotate without restraint. Classify tissue, identify articular geometry and then describe the permitted movement with its axis and stabilizers.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: Bone shape predicts broad mechanical roles, but size alone does not define the category: phalanges are long bones despite being small. Fibrous connections use connective tissue, primary cartilaginous joints use hyaline cartilage, and symphyses contain fibrocartilage between bony surfaces. A synostosis is fusion by bone and can develop from an earlier connection. Classify the connecting tissue before describing the amount of movement, because structural and functional classifications answer different questions.
